draft.title: Obedience and Milgram
card: Obedience is following a direct order from a person seen as an authority. It differs from conformity, where people match a group without being told to.
In the 1960s, Stanley Milgram told volunteers to give electric shocks to a learner each time the learner answered wrongly. The shocks were not real, but the volunteers believed they were.
The shocks rose up to a level labelled as dangerous. About two thirds of volunteers went all the way to the highest level when the experimenter told them to continue.
Many volunteers showed stress, but kept going. Milgram concluded that ordinary people can obey an authority even when the order harms someone else.
draft.remember: Obedience is following an authority's orders. Most of Milgram's volunteers obeyed, even when they believed they were hurting someone.

a.q: What did most volunteers in Milgram's study do?
opts: Kept giving what they thought were shocks when told to
Refused to give any shock at all after the first request
Stopped once the learner first said the answer was wrong
Copied what the other volunteers in the room were doing
a.why: Most volunteers kept giving what they believed were shocks because the experimenter told them to continue. Copying other volunteers would be conformity, but Milgram's study tested obedience to an authority's direct orders.
a.clue: Think about who was giving the orders.

b.q: A coach tells a player to run extra laps. The player is tired but runs them because the coach said so. Which idea does this show?
opts: Obedience, as the player follows an authority's order
Conformity, as the player matches what a group does
Obedience, as the player copies the rest of the team
Conformity, as the player follows an order from the coach
b.why: The coach is an authority who gave a direct order, and the player followed it. That is obedience. Conformity involves changing behaviour to match a group, with no order given.
b.clue: Was there a direct order from someone in charge?

a.best: Kept giving what they thought were shocks when told to

b.best: Obedience, as the player follows an authority's order
